current_law_statement: Sessions reviewed: 2024 (125th, 2nd), 2025 and 2026 (126th) Acts lists on scstatehouse.gov; the codified S.C. Code (scstatehouse.gov, stated current through the 2025 session) shows § 30-4-30 last amended by 2017 Act No. 67 (eff. May 19, 2017), and no 2024–2026 act touching FOIA fees was found. S. 6 (2025-2026), which would rewrite § 30-4-30(C) response timing, re-states subsection (B) verbatim and remains in Senate Judiciary (introduced Jan. 14, 2025) — not law. All fee/payment content is in § 30-4-30(B)–(C); SC has no FOIA fee regulation (Code of Regulations checked) and no statewide uniform fee schedule. Guidance-vs-law gap: the AG/Press Association 'Public Official's Guide' (2003 amendments edition) quotes the pre-2017 fee text and is superseded; the AG's FOIA web page publishes only the AG office's own schedule. AG opinions opened (2019, 2020, 2024) construe waiver discretion and record-creation fees but set no figures.

resolutions.value: prevailing commercial rate for the producing of copies
resolutions.unit: USD per page (city sets under the standard)
resolutions.source_language: Fees charged by a public body must be uniform for copies of the same record or document and may not exceed the prevailing commercial rate for the producing of copies. The public body shall develop a fee schedule to be posted online.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (2017 Act No. 67, eff. May 19, 2017; no later amendment through 2025 session; no 2026 act found)
resolutions.notes: No cents-per-page figure anywhere in SC law; the copy fee is bounded by a non-numeric ceiling ('prevailing commercial rate') and must be uniform for the same record and posted in the body's online fee schedule (city sets the number). 'Public body' expressly includes municipalities (§ 30-4-20(a)). Guidance only, not binding on cities: the AG's own-office schedule charges $0.20/page; the 2020 SC OIG survey benchmarked commercial self-service B&W copies at $0.08–$0.14 (Apr. 2019). Existing row SC-0009 records the same clause with constraint_basis=ceiling — a non-numeric ceiling; treated here as actual_cost_standard because no number can be extracted.

resolutions.notes: No oversized/nonstandard-size rule anywhere in the chapter; the general copy ceiling ('prevailing commercial rate for the producing of copies') is the only constraint. Recorded as the general standard, not a distinct oversized rule.

No specialty schedule exists in statute, regulation or AG guidance. AG (2019, restating 1996) states a body is not required to create a record (e.g., a transcript) but may, with fees governed by § 30-4-30(B).

resolutions.value: prorated hourly salary of the lowest paid employee who, in the reasonable discretion of the custodian, has the necessary skill and training to perform the request
resolutions.unit: USD per hour (formula ceiling; computed per body)
resolutions.source_language: The fee for the search, retrieval, or redaction of records shall not exceed the prorated hourly salary of the lowest paid employee who, in the reasonable discretion of the custodian of the records, has the necessary skill and training to perform the request. The public body may establish and collect reasonable fees not to exceed the actual cost of the search, retrieval, and redaction of records.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (2017 Act No. 67, eff. May 19, 2017; no later amendment through 2025 session; no 2026 act found)
resolutions.notes: Ceiling is a computed figure, not a dollar amount: the body's own prorated hourly salary of the lowest-paid employee with the necessary skill and training (custodian's reasonable discretion). Outer bound: reasonable fees 'not to exceed the actual cost of the search, retrieval, and redaction'. City supplies the salary-derived rate under the cap. Binds all public bodies incl. municipalities. AG's own office charges $19.00/hr (agency procedure, not binding on cities).

new_rules.legal_concept: Public-interest fee waiver/reduction is discretionary; clause reaches local governmental bodies (AG reading)
new_rules.atomic_rule: A finding that disclosure is in the public interest, supporting a fee waiver or reduction under § 30-4-30(B), is discretionary on the part of the agency; a requestor might not be granted a waiver or reduction, and the AG reads the undefined term 'agency' as likely applying to local governmental bodies as well as state bodies.
new_rules.trigger: Requester seeks waiver or reduction of fees on public-interest grounds
new_rules.source_language: However, finding that a disclosure is in the public interest is discretionary on the part of the agency and the requestor might not be granted a waiver or reduction from the fee schedule. [footnote 1:] Because the term "agency" is not modified in S.C. Code Ann. § 30-4-30(B), a court may well hold it applies to state bodies as well as local governmental bodies, including school districts.
new_rules.source_authority: Op. S.C. Att'y Gen. to Rep. Forrest & Councilman Hudson (June 28, 2019), construing S.C. Code Ann. § 30-4-30(B)
new_rules.notes: Advisory only; SC AG opinions are not binding. Adds the applies_to judgment (local bodies covered) and the discretionary character; the operative statutory clause is SC-0015. Also confirms the General Assembly-member exception is not extended to other legislative bodies.

new_rules.legal_concept: Fees for a record the public body elects to create are governed by § 30-4-30(B)
new_rules.atomic_rule: A public body is not required to create a record that does not exist by extracting information from other documents, but may create such a document for a requestor if it chooses; the fees it may charge for doing so are governed by § 30-4-30(B).
new_rules.trigger: Requester asks for a compilation/extraction/transcript that does not exist and the body elects to create it
new_rules.source_language: The public body is not required to create a record where the record does not otherwise exist by extracting information from other documents which are in the possession of the public body. On the other hand, the public body may create such a document for a requestor if it chooses; the fees which may be charged by the public body for doing so would be governed by §30-4-30(b).
new_rules.source_authority: Op. S.C. Att'y Gen. (June 28, 2019), quoting Op. S.C. Att'y Gen., 1996 WL 190741 (Mar. 5, 1996)

applicability_notes: 'Public body' (§ 30-4-20(a)) expressly includes 'counties, municipalities, townships, school districts, and special purpose districts' — every § 30-4-30(B)-(C) figure/standard binds municipalities directly (applies_to = all_public_bodies).
The waiver clause uses the undefined term 'agency'; AG Op. June 28, 2019 reads it as likely covering local governmental bodies — waiver branch applied to municipalities on that basis (SC-9001).

AG office schedule ($19.00/hr; $0.20/page; $12.00/hr conversion) and the 2020 SC OIG state-agency FOIA survey (copy fees $0.05–$0.50; commercial benchmark $0.08–$0.14) are state-agency figures — guidance only, never a municipal value.
Deposit ceiling base is 'total reasonably anticipated cost for reproduction' — narrower wording than total estimated cost; flagged on rules.deposit.percent.
The 'lowest-paid qualified employee prorated hourly salary' cap names search, retrieval and redaction only; whether it also caps format-conversion 'staff time' (SC-0012) is unresolved.
material_negatives: No statewide per-page copy rate (B&W, color, oversized) — only the non-numeric 'prevailing commercial rate' ceiling plus uniformity.
No labor rate figure — a salary-formula ceiling; no billing increment, no free hours, no periodic free allowance, no overhead/fringe authorization.
No estimate regime: no itemized-estimate threshold, requester response window, revision trigger or validity period.
No deposit dollar threshold (deposit permitted at discretion, capped at 25%); no nonpayment withdrawal, prior-debt, overrun/re-issue or payment-method rule.
No de-minimis, minimum fee, media, delivery/postage, certification, audio/video, commercial-purpose, fee-forfeiture or repeat/aggregation rule.
No FOIA fee regulation exists in the S.C. Code of Regulations; no AG opinion found setting or construing a fee figure since the 2017 rewrite.
